html:
The Atikum are an Indigenous people of the Serra do Umã, a range of hills in the dry backlands of Pernambuco, northeast Brazil. Their land lies in the caatinga scrub, where they farm beans, maize and manioc.

Little is known of the peoples of these hills before the cattle ranchers of Portuguese Brazil moved in. Their old language was lost long ago. In the 1940s the Atikum won recognition from the state by performing the toré, a ritual dance shared with neighbours like the Pankararu. Several thousand Atikum live in Brazil today.
